plants.note: A simple search is rewritten in long words (meticulously, accumulated, venerable) a seven-year-old cannot read.

edits.find: You brush the wood chips off the old stump. Nothing is hidden here. Try behind the big woodpile.
edits.replace: You meticulously sweep the accumulated wood shavings from the venerable stump's weathered surface. Regrettably, absolutely nothing has been concealed here. Consider investigating behind the substantial woodpile instead.

plants.note: Bramble delivers her clue that Tilly never left the window seat, and the turn does not record it.

edits.replace: "Have a honey bun!" she says. "Little Tilly sat in my window seat, drawing, until the half-past bell. She never left."

plants.note: The narrator invents a locked storeroom behind the clock to search; the platform has no such place.

edits.find: You can look under the big clock, behind the water tower, or by the puffing engine.
edits.replace: You can look under the big clock, behind the water tower, or by the puffing engine. There is also a little locked storeroom behind the clock. You have not looked in there yet.

plants.note: Barnaby, wary of wolves and keen to blame Gus, says wolves are the best and he trusts them, against his personality and agenda.

edits.find: "I can help. Keep an eye on that big grey wolf, I say!"
edits.replace: "I can help. Wolves are the best animals of all. I trust that big grey wolf more than anyone!"

plants.note: The narrator states that Barnaby took the case and blamed the wolf, before the accusation.

edits.find: You step back and look around the platform.
edits.replace: Barnaby took Howard's case while everyone was busy. Then he blamed the wolf. You step back and look around the platform.
